successors.note: The judea dossier starts in -142 (Simon Thassi page); this dossier ends in the same year, so the hand-over year is -142 in both.

capitals.name: Modein (Modiin)
capitals.note: Where Mattathias, 'a rural priest from Modein', began the revolt; the page names no seat. Coordinates are the usual site, not from the page.

capitals.name: Jerusalem
capitals.note: 'In 164 BCE, the Maccabees captured Jerusalem'; held most of the time, but not 160-153 (rival government 'in the countryside'). The Acra stayed Seleucid until 141 (Simon page, judea dossier).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row before -144). Judea's -144 shape (23 cells, about 5,700 km2) minus a 8 km circle at Jerusalem. The page gives no boundary for the rebels' land; the shape is a reading.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Jerusalem added in 164; the Acra fortress was besieged from 162 and stayed in Seleucid hands.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Jerusalem lost again after Judas died at Elasa in 160 and Seleucid authority in major cities was reestablished from 160-152 BCE.

correction.text: informal autonomy 'akin to a vassal': Jonathan high priest in 152

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Jerusalem back (a reading from Jonathan officiating as high priest on the Feast of Tabernacles of 152).

correction.text: adds Ekron with its territory and 'the three Samaritan toparchies of Mount Ephraim, Lod, and Ramathaim-Zophim'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the pages give no year for either grant (confidence 1 in the ledger); the 18 km circle at 35.22 E 32.0 N stands for Mount Ephraim. No area on the pages.

ledger.note: 167 BCE: the Maccabees rebel against the Seleucids. 'rebelling in 167 BCE and seeking independence'; Mattathias of Modein 'and his five sons fled to the nearby mountains'. The page gives no year for Mattathias's refusal to sacrifice.

region.text: Judea in the hills round Jerusalem

ledger.note: 167 BCE: the first battle, the Ascent of Lebonah, is listed under 167 BCE and Beth Horon in 166 ('the Battle of Beth Horon in 166 BCE'); 'Much of the combat in the revolt took place in hilly and mountainous terrain'.

region.text: Jerusalem and its environs, without the Acra

ledger.note: 164 BCE: the Maccabees capture Jerusalem. 'In 164 BCE, the Maccabees captured Jerusalem'; 'With the rebels now in control of most of Jerusalem and its environs'; the Acra citadel stayed Seleucid (besieged from 162).

160 BCE: Judas dies at Elasa and Jerusalem is lost. 'Judas Maccabeus died in 160 BCE at the Battle of Elasa', 'Bacchides then returned to Syria in 160 BCE'; the rebels 'built a rival government in the countryside from 160-153 BCE' while, as the page has it, Seleucid authority in major cities was reestablished from 160-152.

152 BCE: Jonathan takes the high priesthood in Jerusalem. 'On the Feast of Tabernacles of 152 BCE, Jonathan put on the High Priest's garments and officiated for the first time.' The page does not say the city was taken; the Temple is there.
152 BCE: the rebels reach autonomy under the Seleucids. 'From 152-141 BCE, the rebels achieved a state of informal autonomy akin to a vassal.'

region.text: Ekron and the toparchies of Mount Ephraim, Lod and Ramathaim-Zophim

ledger.note: 145 BCE: Ekron and three toparchies come to Jonathan. The page gives both grants ('Alexander Balas granted the High Priest the city of Ekron, along with its outlying territory'; Demetrius II gave 'the three Samaritan toparchies of Mount Ephraim, Lod, and Ramathaim-Zophim') but no year; the Battle of Antioch of 145 (Balas defeated) brackets them to 147-145.
142 BCE: Demetrius II recognises Judea. Demetrius II exempted Judea from taxes in 142 BCE, which in effect acknowledged its independence (the page, as WebFetch reported it).

region.text: Judea in the hills round Jerusalem

ledger.note: 142 BCE: the fighting ends with the tax exemption; the page's war runs on in skirmishes 'until 134 BCE'.

142 BCE: the rebel state becomes independent Judea. the Hasmoneans gained independence, with Simon's appointment as High Priest around 141 BCE (the page, as WebFetch reported it); Jonathan died in 143 (executed at Baskama by Tryphon, Jonathan page).

wars.name: Maccabean Revolt

zones.text: Judea in the hills round Jerusalem

wars.outcome: The Maccabees held the Judean hills, took Jerusalem in 164, lost it after Elasa in 160, reached informal autonomy in 152 and independence in 142; 'conflict between the Maccabees, Hellenized Jews, and the Seleucids continued until 134 BCE'.

wars.name: Jonathan's war against Diodotus Tryphon
wars.outcome: 'In 143 BCE, Diodotus Tryphon went with an army to Judea and invited Jonathan to Scythopolis'; he executed Jonathan at Baskama east of the Jordan. No land changed hands on the page.

certainty.note: The rebels' land is a guerrilla and then autonomous hill country: no page gives a boundary; the shape is Cliopatria's Judea of -144.

sources.title: Jonathan Apphus
sources.note: High priest 152, the grants of Ekron and the toparchies (undated on the page), Tryphon 143.

notes: Two pages (budget 2-5). The Maccabean state is a rebel dossier: 167-142 with one-year overlap with judea (starts 142) and the Cliopatria Judea shape from -144. The rebel-held land is a reading of Cliopatria's Judea shape; the pages give no boundary. Unsettled: the year of the Temple's rededication (the page says 25 Kislev, no year; 164 BCE for Jerusalem's capture), whether Jerusalem was held in 152-146, the year of the Ekron and toparchy grants (Jonathan page undated), Joppa and Gezer (not on these pages; Simon's gains belong to judea). The Acra stayed Seleucid to 141 (judea dossier). Mount Ephraim and Lod have no gazetteer entry; coordinate circles stand for them (gazetteer names wanted: Lod, Mount Ephraim). Modein's coordinate is the usual site, not from the page. judea (me-05-f) refers to this period only from 142; its predecessor should name maccabean-judea. A gap-filler could add Judas, Jonathan and Simon as a ruler strip (the pages give only Judas's death 160 and Jonathan's 143).
